study.comments: Table 1 is titled 'in vitro antifungal susceptibility' but the text states that its percentages are resistance rates (e.g. 'C. tropicalis showed 100% resistance to fluconazole and itraconazole'); I treated them as % resistant. Resistance is implausibly high for all species and agents (>80% except amphotericin B), and CLSI M44 has no zone criteria for clotrimazole, nystatin, ketoconazole or itraconazole, so the categories are questionable. The C. tropicalis denominator is 15 in the results and Table 1 but 16 in the phospholipase discussion (5/16). No MICs are reported. The main aim is virulence factors and E. cardamomum activity.

The text gives only that nystatin was 100% susceptible in C. tropicalis (among other species), and the discussion says that 'all our identified species were resistant to Fluconazole', which contradicts the overall fluconazole susceptibility of 14.42% in the abstract. n_candida_total = 99 (75 C. albicans + 10 C. tropicalis + 6 C. krusei + 4 C. famata + 4 C. sake), calculated from the counts; 127 fungal isolates in total, including Cryptococcus. study.comments: Only non-albicans Candida were collected (no C. albicans). The susceptibility percentages for C. tropicalis (fluconazole 4.3% S, posaconazole 3.9% S) are inconsistent with the MIC data in Table 2 (fluconazole MIC50 2 µg/mL, which is S under M60; posaconazole MIC50 0.031), and voriconazole is reported as 100% S although the MIC range reaches 0.6 µg/mL (above the S breakpoint of ≤0.12). The abstract (caspofungin 10% S overall) is also implausible. Counts were calculated from % with n=231. Resistant counts are not given. Isolates from all sources are pooled. The ANF MIC50 (0.016) is lower than the bottom of the reported range (0.0312).

clade4.evidence: this eBURST group of the four azoles resistant isolates also included the resistant isolates from Taiwan and China identified previously (Chou et al., 2007; Fan et al., 2017). This implied that this eBURST group 3 is strongly associated with the triazole resistance of Asian C. tropicalis isolates.
clade4.note: The authors call it 'eBURST group 3', not 'clade 4'; equivalence with the azole-resistant clade 4 is inferred from its inclusion of the Taiwan/China resistant isolates. The 9 resistant isolates are resistant/NWT to all four triazoles. The DSTs of the group are not listed in the text (figures only).

dynamics.description: Proportion of C. tropicalis among candidaemia isolates at Siriraj Hospital rose from 28.0% (2006–2009; Boonyasiri et al. 2013) to 46.7% (2012–2018; 41.1–48.7% per year; 2,048 Candida blood isolates in 2012–2018)
Fluconazole resistance in C. tropicalis rose from 0% (1999–2002, earlier Thai study by Foongladda et al. 2004) to 43.8% in this study; the comparison is with an external study
